classification.habitat: Dry deciduous and thorn forests, roadsides and villages; tolerant of poor and dry soils.
classification.distribution: Throughout India up to about 900 m, wild and widely planted, especially in dry regions.

identification.description: Large evergreen tree with pinnate leaves, serrated leaflets, small fragrant white flowers and yellow ripe drupes.
identification.whole_plant: Moderate-sized to large evergreen tree, 12–15 m high, with a stout trunk and wide spreading crown.
identification.root: Deep, strong tap root with lateral roots.
identification.stem: Stout straight trunk with spreading branches; wood reddish-brown and hard.
identification.leaf: Imparipinnate (or paripinnate) compound leaves, rachis 15–25 cm; leaflets opposite, lanceolate, oblique at base, serrate, 7–8.5 cm long; taste bitter.
identification.flower: Small white, fragrant, honey-scented flowers in axillary drooping panicles.
identification.fruit: Ovoid one-seeded drupe, green turning yellow on ripening, with sweetish-bitter pulp.
identification.seed: Single ellipsoid seed with a hard shell enclosing an oily kernel (source of neem oil).
identification.bark: Bark thick, rough, fissured and rusty-grey outside; inner surface yellowish and laminated; fracture fibrous; taste bitter.
identification_points: Pinnate leaves with oblique-based serrate leaflets
Intensely bitter taste of all parts
Small white fragrant flowers in panicles
Rough fissured grey bark with fibrous fracture

therapeutics.dose: Leaf churna 1–3 g; stem-bark churna 2–4 g
therapeutics.precautions: Tikta-Ruksha and Sheeta; prolonged or high-dose internal use can aggravate Vata and cause weakness. Bark decoction is used mainly externally per API.
therapeutics.contraindications: Neem seed oil must not be given internally to infants and children (reports of serious toxicity). Avoid internal use in pregnancy, in those trying to conceive and in marked Vata states or debility.

shlokas:
निम्बः शीतो लघुर्ग्राही कटुपाकोऽग्निवातकृत्।
अहृद्यः श्रमतृट्कासज्वरारुचिकृमिप्रणुत्॥
व्रणपित्तकफच्छर्दिकुष्ठहृल्लासमेहनुत्॥

निम्बपर्णं स्मृतं नेत्र्यं कृमिपित्तविषप्रघुत् ।
वातलं कटुपाकं च सवरीचकुष्ठनुत् ॥७५॥

निम्बफलं रसे तिक्तं पाके तु कटुभेदनम् ।
स्निग्धं लघुष्णं कुष्ठघ्नं गुल्मार्शःकृमिमेहनुत् ॥७६॥

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: API lists triterpenoids and sterols in the leaf and the bitter principles nimbin and nimbiol in the bark; limonoids such as azadirachtin are concentrated in the seed.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Neem leaf, bark and seed extracts show antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, antifungal and insecticidal activities in laboratory studies; human evidence is limited to small trials (e.g., dental and skin preparations).
recognized_uses: Antiseptic in skin and oral care products
Neem oil and azadirachtin as natural insecticides
Traditional use in skin diseases and wounds
modern_information.safety_notes: Neem oil ingestion has caused metabolic acidosis, seizures and encephalopathy in infants; leaf preparations should not be used long-term or in pregnancy without supervision.
